_about: Hand-written judgement for php-src's work-in-motion map: each quote as php-src's maintainers wrote it (CONTRIBUTING.md, the php/policies repository, accepted RFCs and the release plan on wiki.php.net), with its source. Areas without a quoted plan group PRs by path only. Paths for the areas follow EXTENSIONS and CODEOWNERS, as ~/dev/php's map extracts them.
general_heading: From CONTRIBUTING.md, the php/policies repository and the PHP 8.6 release plan

general.text: If an open pull request already addresses the problem, help test or review it to make it better instead of opening an equivalent pull request.
When multiple pull requests provide equivalent fixes of comparable quality, we follow a first-come, first-served principle. We prefer the first correct pull request.
If you are fixing a bug, then please submit your PR against the lowest actively supported branch of PHP that the bug affects
Pull requests implementing RFCs should be submitted against `master`.

Internal API changes (those that do not affect the user-facing API), as well as user-facing features in extensions and SAPIs, do not require an RFC unless a core developer (someone with commit access to php-src) raises an objection or requests an RFC within one month of the implementation pull request being opened.
general.source: php/policies release-process.rst, Feature selection and development

general.text: Security fixes, compatibility build fixes, fixes to address regressions introduced during a normal bug fix release, and fixes for crashes like use after free or segmentation faults.
general.source: php/policies release-process.rst, what a branch takes in its third year (PHP-8.3 now)

general.text: Hard feature freeze: features, whether requiring an RFC or not, must be merged only with approval from the RMs.

streams.title: URI
streams.summary: ext/uri landed in PHP 8.5; its follow-up RFC is accepted and partly implemented.

target.text: This RFC proposes a set of follow-up improvements to the URL Parsing API RFC.
target.source: Followup Improvements for ext/uri RFC (accepted), Introduction

streams.title: Resources to objects
streams.summary: Each remaining resource type is to become an object; a new resource type goes the other way.

target.text: As eliminating resources altogether should be a strategic goal for PHP
target.source: Resource to object conversion RFC (accepted), Discussion

streams.title: Zend engine
streams.summary: The language engine: compiler, executor, VM, garbage collector, allocator.

streams.summary: ext/opcache, including the JIT and its optimizer.

streams.title: Server APIs
streams.summary: CLI, FPM, CGI, Apache's handler, embed, LiteSpeed and phpdbg.

streams.title: Database extensions

streams.title: XML extensions
streams.summary: dom, libxml, simplexml, soap, xml, xmlreader, xmlwriter and xsl, which EXTENSIONS marks Orphan, and lexbor.

target.text: EXTENSIONS has listed eight of these as Orphan since 2026-04-12, and as Odd fixes before that (soap for longer; the other seven from 2026-02-16); CODEOWNERS still names a reviewer for each of the eight, and work goes on (ext/dom: 96 commits by 26 authors in the 12 months to 2026-10-24).
target.source: our reading of EXTENSIONS, CODEOWNERS and git log (~/dev/php map, 20-machinery/areas.md)
